in_english.name: Eleutherius
in_english.meaning: Name means freedom, liberty, release, or deliverance
in_english.long_meaning: Originating from Greek root Ἕλευσμα (eleusma), meaning freedom, liberty, release. Eleutherius is a name associated with Saint Eleutherius, a 2nd-century bishop of Rome, known for his role in resolving the Quartodeciman controversy. This name symbolizes spiritual freedom, deliverance, and salvation. In Christian tradition, the name Eleutherius is associated with courage, resilience, and perseverance.

data.cultural_impact: St. Eleutherius is recognized as a patron saint of freedom and liberation. In the Middle Ages, he was invoked during regional uprisings to protect the inhabitants in their fight for independence. His feast day on the 22nd of October has been celebrated historically with feasts, prayers, and various rituals while groups struggled for their freedom.
data.spiritual_significance: Christians believe that St. Eleutherius embodies the essence of the Gospel message and shining a light onto the spiritual freedoms that are derived from a close relationship with God. Freedom from sin, fear, and despair, ultimately leading one to grow closer to the divine, and to live a more authentic, compassionate, and loving life. This corresponds to the spiritual freedom Christ alluded to in John 8:32, "If you continue in my word, you are truly my disciples; and you will know the truth, and the truth will make you free."

historical_references.reference: Saint Eleutherius was bishop of the ancient city of Illyricum, in the Roman province of Pannonia Inferior, in the 4th century.
